title: Squares with no digit 7
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: Count the numbers n up to x whose square, written in base 10, has no digit 7. Show that the count has the size the random-digit model predicts.
math: Let $\mathcal A=\{m\ge1:\ \text{the decimal expansion of }m\text{ contains no digit }7\}$. Prove that $\#\{n\le x:\ n^2\in\mathcal A\}=x^{\,1+2\log_{10}(9/10)+o(1)}$ as $x\to\infty$ (exponent $\approx0.9085$). The lower bound $\ge x^{1+2\log_{10}(9/10)-o(1)}$ is the main difficulty; even an asymptotic for the count in some fixed base $q\le 10$ would be new.
